blocks.text: Disappointed, K. took the letter and put it into his pocket. Even in the most favorable case, the advantage that the recommendation could bring him was comparatively smaller than the harm that lay in the fact that the manufacturer knew of his trial and that the painter was spreading the news further. He could scarcely force himself to thank the manufacturer, who was already on his way to the door, with a few words. “I shall go there,” he said, as he took leave of the manufacturer at the door, “or else, since I am very busy just now, write to him that he might come to me at the office sometime.” “I knew, of course,” said the manufacturer, “that you would find the best way out. To be sure, I thought that you would prefer to avoid inviting people like this Titorelli into the Bank in order to speak with him here about the trial. Nor is it always advantageous to let letters pass out of one’s hands to such people. But you have certainly thought everything through and know what you may do.” K. nodded and accompanied the manufacturer on through the anteroom. Yet despite his outward calm he was deeply alarmed at himself. That he would write to Titorelli he had really said only in order to show the manufacturer in some way that he knew how to value the recommendation and was immediately considering the possibilities of meeting with Titorelli, yet if he had regarded Titorelli’s assistance as valuable, he would not have hesitated actually to write to him either. The dangers, however, that this could entail he had recognized only through the manufacturer’s remark. Could he indeed already rely so little upon his own judgment? If it was possible that he might invite a questionable person into the Bank by an explicit letter in order to ask advice of him regarding his trial, separated only by a door from the Deputy Director, was it not then possible and even very probable that he was overlooking other dangers as well or running headlong into them? Not always did someone stand beside him to warn him. And precisely now, when he meant to step forward with all his strength gathered, doubts of this kind about his own vigilance, hitherto alien to him, had to make their appearance! Were the difficulties that he felt in carrying out his office work now to begin in the trial as well? Now, to be sure, he no longer understood at all how it had been possible that he had wanted to write to Titorelli and invite him into the Bank.

He was still shaking his head over it when the attendant stepped to his side and drew his attention to three gentlemen who were sitting here in the anteroom on a bench. They had already been waiting a long time to be admitted to K. Now, since the attendant was speaking with K., they had stood up, and each wanted to take advantage of a favorable opportunity to get to K. ahead of the others. Since so little consideration had been shown on the part of the Bank in letting them waste their time here in the waiting room, they too no longer wished to show any consideration. “Chief Clerk,” one of them was already saying. But K. had had the attendant bring him his winter coat and, while putting it on with the attendant’s help, said to all three: “Forgive me, gentlemen, unfortunately I have no time at this moment to receive you. I beg your pardon most sincerely, but I have an urgent business errand to attend to and must leave at once. After all, you have seen for yourselves how long I have just been detained. Would you be so kind as to come back tomorrow or whenever you wish? Or shall we perhaps discuss the matters by telephone? Or would you perhaps care to tell me briefly just now what it is about, and I shall then give you a detailed written answer. The best thing, to be sure, would be if you came again shortly.” These proposals of K.’s threw the gentlemen, who were now supposed to have waited completely in vain, into such astonishment that they looked at one another in silence. “So we are agreed?” asked K., who had turned toward the attendant, who was now bringing him his hat as well. Through the open door to K.’s room one could see how much heavier the snowfall outside had grown. K. therefore turned up his coat collar and buttoned it high under his throat.
